Several of us were discussing some interesting (single-value) `<select>` sizing behavior yesterday: [testcase](https://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?%3C!DOCTYPE%20html%3E%0A%3Cselect%3E%0A%3Coption%3EShort%3C%2Foption%3E%0A%3Coption%3ELooooooooooooooooooooong%3C%2Foption%3E%0A%3C%2Fselect)

This isn't currently implementable in CSS, because the content is taken out of flow. To do it, we would need the button to contain all the values always, and just [collapse](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-flexbox/#visibility-collapse) the ones that aren't selected so that they are invisible, but still in-flow and contributing to the size of the button. (Notably, we don't want to take the size of the popover, we want to take the size of the content as it would be represented if it were selected.)

Bringing that up here because it's also potentially about representing multiple items in `<selectedcontent>`.

@josepharhar I don't see a response here to https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12342#issuecomment-4565525487 which I think is important to consider at least. We could make `selectedcontent` contain a clone of all `option` elements and make them match `:checked` as needed.

> This isn't currently implementable in CSS, because the content is taken out of flow. To do it, we would need the button to contain all the values always, and just [collapse](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-flexbox/#visibility-collapse) the ones that aren't selected so that they are invisible, but still in-flow and contributing to the size of the button. (Notably, we don't want to take the size of the popover, we want to take the size of the content as it would be represented if it were selected.)
> 
> Bringing that up here because it's also potentially about representing multiple items in `<selectedcontent>`.

I think that this is worth a separate issue and in my opinion doesn't need to block selectedcontent in select multiple. If we only include the dom of the selected option(s), then the obvious way to do selectedcontent in select multiple is to include the dom of each selected option element, like my current proposal does. If we end up changing the selectedcontent element to always include the dom of each option element, then we would be making the same change for single select and multi select selectedcontent elements.

I don't agree. Not needing a toggle for multiple select would be rather nice. And multiple select forces the question of how you represent multiple options so we might as well go with the solution we'd want for that instead of having multiple ways of representing multiple options.

Ok, let me see if I understand. Here's what a single select would look like:
```html
<select>
  <button>
    <selectedcontent>
      <clonedoption>one</clonedoption>
      <clonedoption>two</clonedoption>
    </selectedcontent>
  </button>
  <option>one</option>
  <option>two</option>
</select>
```
And you would have this UA css to make it so that only one of them is rendered in a way where they all still get laid out:
```css
clonedoption:not(:selected) {
  visibility: collapse;
}
selectedcontent {
  /* needed to make visibility:collapse work? */
  display: flex;
}
```
Does that sound right?

Thanks for the example Anne!

I think that reusing the option element would be tricky because we would need to:
1. Rewrite algorithms which collect descendant options of a select element to skip over the ones inside selectedcontent elements
2. Make sure that interaction behaviors don't do anything weird, like clicking the cloned options shouldn't activate anything about the option or select, but as Luke pointed out the inertness should hopefully take care of that
3. Make sure that options are rendered as if they are regular divs instead of having the styles that we give to options inside select elements. Not sure if its easy to change the CSS selectors which target options inside select elements, and we might also need to change the way that the base appearance bit is propagated in computed style from selects to option elements.

Another issue is that if you're constructing the DOM of a select element imperatively from script, then naively we would have to reclone the entire selectedcontent element every time an option is added, even if that option is not selected. I imagine this would lead to bad performance in common cases. If we waited a microtask before doing this cloning, then that should address it. Using more microtasks might go against how some people felt in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10520 but we already added more microtasks in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12263 so maybe thats ok?

> If #12050 happens then selectedcontent could exist outside of an inert tree and that might get trickier?

In that case the options shouldn't have any ancestor select element so they should already act and render as regular divs.

1. Per https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/13038 it seems we'll have to do that anyway.
2. I haven't noticed any issues in WebKit's prototype implementation.
3. I think we mostly want to match styles? The only thing I ended up doing on top was to hide the unselected options by default: https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/commit/276ff916b54c07e8a3b69ab6c509899a10fa9976 @fantasai did suggest that we probably want something better than `display: none` here, but I'm not sure I can explain that as well as she can.
4. I've used microtasks that can be invalidated. An alternative would be trying to keep the two trees fully synchronized, but that seems more fragile. I'm also not cloning when the user makes a selection, then I do synchronize.

I don't see any advatage of using `<option>` over `<div>`/`<span>`/`<data value="">`/`<clonedoption>`...
It would even be annoying to write a complex selector just to style an `<option>` that's not in `<selectedcontent>`.

> I think we mostly want to match styles? The only thing I ended up doing on top was to hide the unselected options by default: WebKit/WebKit@276ff91 @fantasai did suggest that we probably want something better than display: none here, but I'm not sure I can explain that as well as she can.

At the very least, they shouldn't have checkmarks should they? And the less styles we apply the more likely it will be compatible with existing usage of the selectedcontent element.

> I've used microtasks that can be invalidated. An alternative would be trying to keep the two trees fully synchronized, but that seems more fragile. I'm also not cloning when the user makes a selection, then I do synchronize.

That's a good point, figuring out which cloned options should match :checked or whatever after selection is changed also could be tricky. How exactly do you figure this out? Do you have a pointer from each option element to its cloned option? Or do you iterate everything in the selectedcontent element and try to figure out which should match which?

> It would even be annoying to write a complex selector just to style an `<option>` that's not in `<selectedcontent>`.

This is a good point, I wonder how many selectors we have in the ua stylesheet that we would have to reconsider should apply to options or their descendants in selectedcontent vs not, and the same thing for author styles that already exist on websites.

> Do you have a pointer from each option element to its cloned option?

I have the reverse and I essentially synchronize all of them when the selection gets invalidated. It's not very optimized thus far.
